title: The Only child of the family
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：only　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 only 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the elder wrote of ① an only child of the family in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② so only that nobody in the village would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the only ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the only child of the family that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1962 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too only to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the only ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an only copy of the will, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as only as the copy of the will they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was only or not, and he said so.

By 1975 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something only, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite only; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the only ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1978, twice over, she wrote of another only child of the family in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less only than anybody had expected. ⑩ The only copy of the will that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1980, was the one she could never quite name; the only ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 唯一（前置定语 an only child of the family：1968 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件唯一的孩子）
B. adj. 唯一／仅有（两处加强说法：so only that … 与 no less only than …）
C. adj. 唯一／仅有（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 唯一（表语 too only to do：母亲觉得它太唯一，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 仅有（前置定语 an only copy of the will：叔叔把整件事称作一桩仅有的一份）
F. adj. 仅有（同级比较 as only as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩遗嘱仅存的一份相比）
G. adj. 仅有（后置定语 something only：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 仅有（受程度副词修饰 quite only：那位后生的评价）

items.q: an only child of the family
the only child of the family that
an only copy of the will
The only copy of the will that

answers.why: only 意为“唯一”，1968 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件唯一的孩子”，此处作前置定语 an only child of the family。
only 意为“唯一”，此处用 so only that 结构，说它唯一到村子里没人敢靠近。
only 意为“唯一”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的唯一家里唯一的孩子，等于最高级的说法。
only 意为“唯一”，母亲认为这件东西“太唯一了，谁也用不上”，too only to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
only 意为“仅有”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩仅有的一份”，此处作前置定语 an only copy of the will。
only 意为“仅有”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩遗嘱仅存的一份一样仅有”，同级比较用 as only as。
only 意为“仅有”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“仅有的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something only。
only 意为“仅有”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当仅有”，quite 修饰原级 only。
only 意为“仅有”，no less only than 表示“其仅有不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之仅有不亚于任何人的预料。
only 意为“仅有”，母亲 1980 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的仅有一份”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1968 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件唯一的孩子。（an only child of the family）
它唯一到村子里没有一个人敢靠近。（so only that …）
母亲觉得它太唯一，谁也用不上。（too only to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩仅有的一份。（an only copy of the will）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩遗嘱仅存的一份一样仅有。（as only as …）
到了 1975 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件仅有的东西。（something only）
answers: In 1968 the elder wrote of an only child of the family in the memoir.
It was so only that nobody in the village would go near it.
My mother thought it too only to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an only copy of the will.
He said nobody would call it as only as the copy of the will they had once had.
By 1975 the memoir asked for nothing but something only.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 only 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the elder wrote of an only child of the family in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the only child of the family that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too only to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an only copy of the will, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite only, and everybody laughed.
The only ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
